note: Monday 28 Sep 2026, ~07:0x SGT, pre-Asia-open re-verification run. All cash markets (US/HKEX/SGX/JPX Fri 25 Sep close, KRX reopening today after Chuseok) remain at levels as of Fri 25 Sep US close (S&P 500 7,743.41 +0.51%, Nasdaq 27,068.72 +0.48%, Dow 51,828.62 +0.93%, Russell 2000 2,837.55 +0.07%, VIX 14.87 -5.1%) -- no new cash session has traded, but the geopolitical and futures picture moved materially over the weekend. Trump publicly rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz-reopening roadmap Sat 26 Sep as 'not acceptable.' Iran's FM Araghchi hardened the line further on Sun 27 Sep: Tehran says it has received no formal channel response from mediators Qatar/Pakistan, will NOT soften its conditions (end of the 'war of aggression,' unfrozen assets, right to sell oil), calls Trump's public remarks 'contradictory,' and says Iran sees 'little reason' to re-engage diplomatically given repeated US strikes -- a materially harder stance than Saturday's 'awaiting a formal response' framing. The ~Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep deadline set by Iran's SNSC looks set to lapse without a deal. Oil moved in an unusual, informative way: Brent plunged -5.39% to $98.70 into Sunday's Globex close on market hopes/rumors that US-Iran talks could still progress -- a speculative unwind of the war-risk premium, NOT an actual Hormuz reopening or supply increase (per FXLeaders) -- while WTI actually rose +1.27% to $93.58, because the physical Strait of Hormuz constraint (vessel traffic still far below pre-war levels) hasn't eased. That Brent/WTI divergence is a risk-premium-vs-physical-supply split, and it looks fragile: early Monday futures/press coverage points to Brent already climbing back and US equity futures softening modestly as markets digest that Iran's harder Sunday tone makes an imminent deal look less likely, not more. Gold ($4,294.40, -0.62%) and silver ($64.18, -0.10%) extended Friday's pullback into Sunday even as the Iran standoff hardened -- the usual safe-haven playbook did not fire this weekend, worth flagging as a genuine anomaly rather than smoothing over. RBA decides Tue 29 Sep 12:30 SGT with markets pricing a ~92-94% probability of a 25bp hike to 4.60% (from 4.35%) after firmer AU inflation; Australia CPI (Wed 30 Sep, y/y forecast accelerating to 4.1% from 3.5%) is the domestic catalyst behind that. US Core PCE + Final GDP (Wed 30 Sep 20:30 SGT, PCE forecast 0.3% vs 0.2% prior) and a heavy Fed-speaker slate (Bowman, Cook, Barkin, Barr, Goolsbee, Musalem, Williams, Waller, Collins, Kashkari) round out the week, building toward the 2 Oct payrolls print (forecast 98K vs 162K prior).

macro.regime: Hawkish-Fed war-shock: Iran deadline lapsing without a deal, oil premium whipsawing
macro.narrative: The regime holds -- hawkish Fed, stressed long-end rates, live Iran/Hormuz war-shock -- but the Iran leg hardened further over the weekend even as headline oil prices swung sharply in the opposite direction, a genuine divergence worth trusting rather than smoothing into a single 'escalation' or 'de-escalation' story. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap Sat 26 Sep; Iran's FM Araghchi doubled down Sun 27 Sep, saying Tehran has received no formal response through mediators, will not soften its conditions, finds Trump's statements 'contradictory,' and sees little reason to re-engage diplomatically after repeated US strikes -- a harder line than Saturday's framing, with the ~Mon-Tue 28-29 Sep deadline now likely to lapse without resolution. Oil's reaction was the week's most informative signal: Brent plunged -5.39% to $98.70 into Sunday's close on market hope that talks could still progress -- a speculative unwind of the risk premium rather than any actual supply increase -- while WTI rose +1.27% to $93.58 because the physical Strait of Hormuz constraint (vessel traffic still far below pre-war norms) hasn't changed; early Monday reports suggest that Brent gap is already partly reversing as markets absorb Iran's harder tone. Gold and silver extended their Friday pullback through the weekend despite the standoff hardening -- the safe-haven playbook simply didn't fire, a notable anomaly that argues for humility on near-term precious-metals direction even though the structural (central-bank buying, supply-deficit) case is intact. This week's dominant scheduled catalysts are the RBA decision (Tue 29 Sep, ~92-94% priced for a 25bp hike to 4.60%) on the back of firmer Australian inflation, US Core PCE and Final GDP (Wed 30 Sep, PCE forecast 0.3% vs 0.2% prior), and a dense Fed-speaker calendar all week, building toward 2 Oct payrolls (forecast 98K, sharply down from 162K). Credit spreads remain historically tight with little cushion if the Iran deadline lapses badly or PCE surprises hot.
